title: When the Prom Wakes
premise: Petra Okonkwo just wants to survive senior year unnoticed at Hollow Creek High, a school built on the flooded ruins of the old Bellhaven Academy. But when a group chat she never joined starts posting messages that predict disasters before they happen—each one signed by a student who died in the 1979 Bellhaven fire—Petra is pulled into an unlikely found family of misfits determined to uncover what the school board buried. As the predictions grow darker and the school board closes ranks, Petra must choose between the safety of invisibility and the truth, even if exposing it costs her everything she's built. In the end, she reveals the board's cover-up at the championship game, frees the trapped spirits by giving them names, and learns that love—for friends, for the dead, for herself—is worth every price survival demands.
about_author: Ada Eastwick grew up in a rust-belt town where the high school sat on land nobody talked about, and she never stopped wondering why. She writes stories about stubborn kids, haunted places, and the families we build when the ones we're given aren't enough.

chapters.title: The Fine Girl
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Three weeks into Hollow Creek High, Petra narrates her careful system of invisibility: sit center-left, laugh on cue, never volunteer. But a guidance counselor's odd questions about 'adjusting' and a janitor who won't mop near the east stairwell rattle her. Beat: loneliness disguised as control, with hairline cracks showing.

chapters.title: Wrong Number
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. She's added to a group chat called 'Bellhaven '79' by an unknown number. The first message predicts a pipe burst in the gym—hours before it floods the floor. Petra tells herself it's a prank. Beat: the first cold drop of dread beneath her practiced calm.

chapters.title: The Misfit Table
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The chat's other members reveal themselves at lunch: Theo, a paranoid AV kid; Marisol, the star athlete hiding a knee injury; and Dev, whose grandmother survived the Bellhaven fire. They've all received predictions. Beat: reluctant connection—found family's awkward first hello.

chapters.title: What the Water Keeps
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev shares his grandmother's story: Bellhaven Academy burned in 1979, and three students were never accounted for. The school board bought the land, flooded the foundations, and built over them. Beat: grief inherited, history as a living thing under the floorboards.

chapters.title: Second Prediction
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The chat warns of a car crash at the corner of Mill Road. Petra and Theo stake it out and watch it happen exactly as described—saving the driver just in time. Beat: terror and awe; the predictions stop being deniable.

chapters.title: Names in the Yearbook
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. In the library's sealed archives, Marisol finds a 1979 Bellhaven yearbook with three photos burned away. The chat sends the names: Ruth, Caleb, and a third it refuses to say. Beat: the dead become people, and the stakes turn personal.

chapters.title: Detention with the Principal
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Principal Vance summons Petra, warning her about 'troublemakers digging up the past.' He offers her a scholarship recommendation in exchange for distance from her new friends. Beat: temptation of the old life—duty to self versus loyalty to others.

chapters.title: East Stairwell, After Hours
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo rigs cameras in the east stairwell where the janitor won't go. The footage shows frost forming in summer, and a handprint that isn't anyone's. Beat: fear sharpening into purpose; the haunting is real and it's asking for something.

chapters.title: Homecoming, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. At homecoming, the chat predicts 'the floor gives way.' Marisol pulls the fire alarm to clear the gym, earning suspension and her coach's fury. Beat: sacrifice—the first real cost paid for strangers, dead or alive.

chapters.title: The Third Name
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev's grandmother, lucid for the first time in years, whispers the third name: her brother, Emeka. Dev realizes the predictions are signed by Ruth, Caleb, and Emeka—the kids the board let burn. Beat: rage and inheritance; this is now family business.

chapters.title: Board Minutes
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra charms her way into the district office and photographs sealed 1980 board minutes referencing 'the Bellhaven settlement.' Vance catches her, but she's already sent copies to Theo. Beat: the invisible girl weaponizes her invisibility.

chapters.title: Cracks in the Group Chat
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The chat starts predicting things about the friends themselves—Marisol's surgery, Theo's expulsion, Petra's transfer. The group fractures over whether the dead are protecting them or using them. Beat: found family under strain; love tested by fear.

chapters.title: What Petra Is Fine About
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Flashback interlude: why Petra learned invisibility—the family she lost, the moves, the promise never to need anyone. She admits to herself she's no longer fine, and doesn't want to be. Beat: the emotional keystone; vulnerability chosen.

chapters.title: The Settlement
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The minutes reveal the board paid the victims' families hush money and sealed a report proving the fire was arson—set by a beloved coach to cover Bellhaven's abuse scandal, with the board's knowledge. Beat: the buried truth surfaces; duty and complicity across generations.

chapters.title: Vance's Offer
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Vance corners Petra: the full scholarship, her mother's job security, everything—if she hands over the documents and names her friends. Petra says no. Beat: love against duty, decided; the door to the old life closes behind her.

chapters.title: Lockdown
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. The board suspends the four, wipes the chat's history, and Dev's grandmother is moved to a facility hours away. The friends regroup in Theo's basement, down but not out, planning to go public before the championship game. Beat: darkest hour, family chosen and holding.

chapters.title: The Last Prediction
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. One final message: 'Friday. The whole school. Don't let them flood it again.' The board plans to pour concrete over the old foundations during championship weekend—permanently entombing the truth. Beat: the clock starts; dread becomes deadline.

chapters.title: Everything We Could Carry
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The four split tasks: Marisol rallies teammates, Dev records his grandmother's testimony, Theo preps the jumbotron feed, Petra writes the speech she swore she'd never give. Beat: quiet courage; each paying a price they've stopped counting.

chapters.title: Championship Night
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. During the final game, Petra takes the field at halftime and broadcasts the settlement, the names, and the arson over the stadium speakers as Theo's feed hijacks the jumbotron. The crowd goes silent, then Vance moves to cut the power. Beat: climax—truth spoken at maximum volume.

chapters.title: The Flood That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. As crews arrive to pour the concrete, hundreds of students, families, and Bellhaven survivors link arms over the east stairwell. The chat sends one last message: three names, then 'thank you,' then nothing. Beat: the dead released; the haunting ends in gratitude.

chapters.title: Memorial
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Spring: the board resigns, the school plants three trees, and the district dedicates a plaque with Ruth, Caleb, and Emeka's names. Petra reads it aloud, voice steady, friends on either side. Beat: grief honored; the price of survival paid forward.

chapters.title: When the Prom Wakes
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. At prom, held in the rebuilt gym, Petra dances with her people, no longer invisible and no longer fine—better than fine. A single message arrives in the old chat: 'Have fun.' Beat: resolution—joy as the hard-won ending, love outlasting duty and death alike.
